findings.text: follow-on: the MCP lifecycle consumer derives severity from the flag alone (severity = "error" if item.flag == "MISSING_IMPL" else "warn") and ignores the LifecycleFinding.severity the change added, so the shipped-plan-in-an-open-sprint row the plan specifies as info is rendered to readers as warn; reckon/project_maintenance_commands.py:1345 _echo_lifecycle_findings is the same gap from the CLI side, printing no severity column at all, so neither surface the change reaches observes the info/warn distinction it added.

follow-on: the added _item_slug is a fourth textual copy of a private sprint-item slug helper the repository already carries at reckon/_store.py:2462 and reckon/roadmap.py:99; the membership index itself is not a fork because its only owner, roadmap._sprint_membership at reckon/roadmap.py:1491, is private and sits in a higher layer (roadmap.py:46 imports doccheck), so extending it would invert the import.

follow-on: the reviewed manifest carries empty baseline_suite and after_suite fields, so the added-failure count derived from it is unmeasured (review.py added_failures_from_gate_logs returns null when either log is absent); its single gate log logs/head_gate.txt is the head arm and its header names the base revision a1ce8441 rather than the head 15129e974, so no log ties the recorded count to the commit the change landed at.

justifications.durability: the two assertions in tests/test_audit_reports_sprint_membership.py:116 and :125 compare emitted slugs against hardcoded expected lists (["b", "c"] warn, ["d"] info) rather than against any value the test passed in, so they redden if the membership comparison is removed or inverted, which logs/negative_control.txt demonstrates; they do not exercise the closed-sprint carve-out or the _item_slug "path" shape.
justifications.evidence: the gate the done-when names, tests/test_audit_reports_sprint_membership.py, passes EXIT=0 on re-run at head, but the reviewed manifest's head gate is EXIT=1 (1 failed) because tests/test_mcp_views.py::test_raw_and_schema_are_explicit_layers (a test importing doccheck through mcp.py) fails on an out-of-scope schema-size bound, and the manifest records no baseline_suite or after_suite log to derive an added-failure count from.
justifications.fit: the change follows the module idiom (a flag constant beside LIFE_CYCLE-style constants, a dataclass field, a per-mount call in audit_lifecycle) and the commit 15129e974 is a conventional subject with a body; no added name carries a plan, sprint, version or ticket label, and the new helpers are named by mechanism (_sprint_membership_finding, sprint_membership_index).
justifications.goal_fidelity: SPRINT_MEMBERSHIP is emitted for both disagreement directions and for the shipped-plan-in-an-open-sprint info case, with the membership read through reckon/project_state.compose_project_state as the plan directed, at reckon/doccheck.py:576 and :606; the plan's "as info" wording is realised on the row's severity field though no consumer surfaces it (recorded as a finding).
justifications.reuse: the membership index has no reachable owner to extend - roadmap._sprint_membership (reckon/roadmap.py:1491) is private and roadmap.py:46 imports doccheck, so extending it would invert the import - and the sprint read is plan-directed through project_state; the defect is the smaller one that the added _item_slug duplicates a private helper already at reckon/_store.py:2462 and reckon/roadmap.py:99.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat a1ce8441..15129e974 touches only reckon/doccheck.py, tests/test_audit_reports_sprint_membership.py and the in-fence evidence fragment, mutates no shared plan, index or sprint state, and leaves the declared figures directory unused.
